original_test_intent: Physically inspect and cycle the specified Mellanox CX8 board, confirm correct slot seating, edge connector, retention, attached cables and clearance, then verify after approved reboot that the same board, ports and links recover without new errors.
original_method: A trained operator binds board part/serial and PCIe identity to the chassis slot, records pre-state photos and Mellanox inventory/link baseline, establishes traffic drain plus ESD/power isolation, removes/reseats the board once per service procedure, restores retention/cables/chassis, then compares board/device/firmware/port/link/driver/error evidence after reboot.
manual_activity: A trained operator inspects and reseats the exact CX8 board, restores retention and dependent cables, and observes reboot/recovery; the owner reviews physical, PCIe and network evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/chassis, CX8 board part/serial/firmware/PCIe identity and exact slot/connector/retention/cable map
Approved board service procedure, workload/traffic drain, cycle count, power-state and ESD requirements
Expected PCIe device, Mellanox port/link/firmware/driver/error state and recovery window
Independent console/network recovery plus spare board/slot escalation plan
Camera/evidence labeling, operator identity and no-log-clear policy
safety_requirements: Only a trained operator may handle the CX8 board under approved traffic-drain, ESD and power-safe controls
Do not remove or insert the board energized unless the service procedure explicitly authorizes this exact platform operation
Stop on wrong board/slot, connector/retention damage, excessive force, unexpected power state, boot/link failure, degraded PCIe/link parameters or new errors
Perform one approved cycle only and diagnose before any repeat
Restore all retention, cables, cooling clearance and chassis closure before power/reboot
agent_execution_scope: Verify row-2006 variant identity and reject copied DC-SCM scope
Collect and compare pre/post PCIe/Mellanox device identity, firmware, port speed/width/FEC, link/driver counters and unfiltered BMC/host errors
Organize board/slot photos, physical-action/reboot timeline and hashes
Flag identity changes, degraded PCIe or network negotiation, missing detection or incomplete physical proof
Perform no board manipulation, seating verdict, reboot authorization or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact board/slot, traffic/workload drain, safe service sequence, cycle count and recovery plan
Ensure trained operator completes physical inspection/reseat and signs the evidence
Review physical, PCIe and network recovery evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed board/slot checklist with pre/post connector, retention, cable and clearance photos, safe drain/isolation confirmation, one-cycle timeline and correlated PCIe, firmware, port/link/driver/counter/error evidence.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The exact XLSX item is Mellanox - CX8 Board, but DeepSeek describes DC-SCM. The primary row and GPT V2 provide coherent board scope, so the copied AI content is isolated rather than treated as source truth.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The authoritative source row is intact and the copied AI scope is repairable by isolation. The case remains MANUAL ONLY with physical execution prerequisites.

review_improvement: Removes the copied DC-SCM procedure, binds the shared code to the CX8 board and adds slot/connector plus PCIe/network recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A CX8 board cycle affects both a PCIe device and multiple network paths. Successful enumeration alone can hide reduced width, missing ports or degraded link negotiation, while network recovery alone cannot prove mechanical retention or edge-connector condition. Thus the evidence must combine physical slot/board identity with PCIe and Mellanox state. The DC-SCM narrative is unsafe here because it targets a different FRU, management function and recovery path.
